## Simple Linear Algebra Functions for Statistics {.unnumbered}


### Description

'broadcast' provides some simple Linear Algebra Functions for Statistics: <br />
<code>cinv()</code>; <br />
<code>sd_gauss_lc()</code>. <br />
<br />
<br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>cinv(x)

sd_gauss_lc(X, vc, bad_rp = NaN)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code></td>
<td>
a real symmetric positive-definite square matrix.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
a numeric matrix of multipliers/constants
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="vc">vc</code></td>
<td>
the variance-covariance matrix for the (correlated) Gaussian random variables.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="bad_rp">bad_rp</code></td>
<td>
if <code>vc</code> is not a Positive (semi-) Definite matrix,
give here the value to replace bad standard deviations with. <br /> <br />
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<b>cinv()</b> <br />
<code>cinv()</code>
computes the Choleski inverse
of a real symmetric positive-definite square matrix. <br />
<br />
<b>sd_gauss_lc()</b> <br />
Given the linear combination <code>X %*% b</code>, where:


<ul>
<li> <code>X</code> is a matrix of multipliers/constants;

</li>
<li> <code>b</code> is a vector of (correlated) Gaussian random variables;

</li>
<li> <code>vc</code> is the variance-covariance matrix for <code>b</code>;

</li></ul>

<code>sd_gauss_lc(X, vc)</code>
computes the standard deviations for the linear combination <code>X %*% b</code>. <br />
Written in 'C' for efficiency. <br />
<br />
<br />



### Value

For <code>cinv()</code>: <br />
A matrix. <br />
<br />
For <code>sd_gauss_lc()</code>: <br />
A vector of standard deviations.
<br />
<br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")


vc <- datasets::ability.cov$cov
X <- matrix(rnorm(1000), 1000, ncol(vc))

solve(vc)
cinv(vc) # faster than `solve()`, but only works on positive definite matrices
all(round(solve(vc), 6) == round(cinv(vc), 6)) # they're the same

sd_gauss_lc(X, vc)

     


```
